message.content:
Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly regarded crime‑thriller films released in 2020 (including limited theatrical releases and streaming debuts). I’ve grouped them by release platform and added a short note on why each one stands out.

| Release Platform | Film | Why It’s Worth Watching |
|------------------|------|--------------------------|
| **Theatrical** | **“The Night Clerk” (Netflix)** | A tense, low‑budget thriller that turns a mundane hotel job into a psychological cat‑and‑mouse game. The film’s claustrophobic atmosphere and strong performances make it a standout in the streaming‑era crime‑thriller niche. |
| | **“The Hunt” (Amazon Prime Video)** | A chilling Danish drama that blends crime investigation with social commentary. Its stark cinematography and morally ambiguous characters keep you guessing until the very end. |
| | **“The Invisible Man” (Hulu)** | Though technically a sci‑fi horror, its plot revolves around a woman being stalked by an unseen antagonist. The film’s pacing and suspenseful twists earned it critical praise. |
| **Streaming** | **“The Trial of the Chicago 7” (Netflix)** | A courtroom drama that doubles as a political thriller. While not a traditional crime‑thriller, its investigative narrative and real‑world stakes give it a gripping edge. |
| | **“The Last Full Measure” (Apple TV+)** | A biographical crime‑drama about a Vietnam veteran who uncovers a cover‑up. The film’s investigative arc and emotional depth make it a compelling watch. |
| | **“The Woman in the Window” (Netflix)** | A psychological thriller that follows a recluse who believes she witnessed a crime. The film’s unreliable narrator and atmospheric tension create a classic “whodunnit” vibe. |
| **Limited Theatrical + Streaming** | **“The Little Things” (Universal Pictures / Peacock)** | Starring Denzel Washington, Rami Malek, and Jared Leto, this procedural thriller explores obsession and moral ambiguity. The film’s gritty tone and strong cast performances earned it positive reviews. |
| | **“The Invisible Man” (Universal Pictures / Peacock)** | A modern retelling of the classic horror story that also functions as a crime‑thriller. The film’s blend of suspense, social commentary, and strong female lead made it a hit. |
| | **“The Hunt” (Universal Pictures / Peacock)** | A Danish crime‑thriller that tackles themes of identity and surveillance. Its tight pacing and strong performances earned it critical acclaim. |

### How to Watch

- **Netflix** – “The Night Clerk,” “The Woman in the Window,” “The Trial of the Chicago 7”
- **Amazon Prime Video** – “The Hunt”
- **Hulu** – “The Invisible Man”
- **Apple TV+** – “The Last Full Measure”
- **Peacock** – “The Little Things,” “The Invisible Man,” “The Hunt”

These titles represent a mix of mainstream releases and indie gems that were praised for their storytelling, direction, and performances. If you’re looking for a crime‑thriller that keeps you on the edge of your seat, any of these should do the trick!
